# {frontmatter.title}

Source: https://github.com/qualcomm/qualcomm-ui/blob/main/packages/docs/qui-docs/src/routes/typedoc.mdx

title: Typedoc

import {TypeDocProps} from "@qualcomm-ui/react-mdx/typedoc"
import {FileTree} from "@qualcomm-ui/react-mdx/file-tree"
import {NpmInstallTabs} from "@qualcomm-ui/react-mdx/npm-install-tabs"

# {frontmatter.title}

## Overview

Our TypeDoc-based parser generates documentation from your TypeScript interfaces and JSDoc comments.

Consider the following example:

```ts
export type WeightUnit = "kg" | "lb"

/**
 * @public
 */
export interface Dog {
  /**
   * The age of the dog in human years.
   */
  age: number

  /**
   * The breed of the dog.
   */
  breed?: string

  /**
   * The name of the dog.
   */
  name: string

  /**
   * The weight of the dog. Refer to {@link weightUnit} for unit type
   * information.
   */
  weight?: number

  /**
   * The unit type of the {@link weight} field.
   *
   * @option `'kg'`: kilograms.
   * @option `'lb'`: pounds.
   */
  weightUnit?: WeightUnit
}
```

Our parser uses [Typedoc](https://typedoc.org/) to consume your package's exports. It produces a JSON model with compiled type definitions. We reference the interface's name in our `TypeDocProps` UI component to render its property documentation table:

```tsx
<TypeDocProps name="Dog" />
```

If you've seen QUI documentation before, this table should look familiar.

<TypeDocProps name="Dog" />

## Features

Our type parser recursively expands type details, including references, so your type documentation is easy to consume. Here are the features:

- JSDoc tag and comment parsing.
- Property linking to other fields from the same interface.
- Union expansion.
- Reference type resolution.
- Property anchor links, including same-page collision resolution.
- Pretty type formatting.
- Required/deprecated property indicators.
- Mobile-first UI components.

## Getting Started

### Install Packages

<NpmInstallTabs dev packages="@qualcomm-ui/typedoc" />

### Initialize the config

Run the command and follow the prompts to generate the config:

```shell
qui-typedoc init
```

### Entry Points

`entryPoints` refer to the root files or directories from which Typedoc will begin the documentation generation process. These are automatically inferred from your `tsconfig` file's `includes` and `files` fields.

You may optionally define `entryPoints` in the typedoc configuration file.

#### QUI Typedoc config

```ts
// qui-typedoc.config.ts
import {BuildOptions} from "@qualcomm-ui/typedoc"

export default {
  // ...
  typedocOptions: {
    // optional. If omitted, the entryPoints will be inferred from
    // the tsconfig's `includes` and `files` fields.
    entryPoints: ["./dist/index.d.ts"],
    tsconfig: "tsconfig.typedoc.json",
  },
} satisfies BuildOptions
```

#### Typedoc tsconfig

```jsonc
// tsconfig.typedoc.json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    // ...
  },
  "include": ["./dist"]
}
```

#### Multiple Entry Points

If your library has a local dependency on another package in your workspace, you will need to list that package in your project's entryPoints. Let's illustrate this scenario with an example.

Consider an example project with the following project structure:

<FileTree
  className="my-4"
  expandedValue={["packages"]}
  onExpandedValueChange={() => {}}
  items={[
    {
      name: "packages",
      items: [
        {name: "base", items: []},
        {name: "react", items: []},
        {name: "react-docs", items: []},
      ],
    },
  ]}
/>

- Assume that `react` has a dependency on `base`.
- Both the `react` and `base` projects compile types to their project's `dist` folder.
- `react-docs` contains the `@qualcomm-ui/typedoc` configuration.

The tsconfig needs to account for both modules:

```jsonc
// packages/react-docs/tsconfig.typedoc.json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    // ...
  },
  "include": ["../base/dist", "../react/dist"]
}
```

If you're specifying entryPoints in the typedoc config, you will also need to account for each module.

#### External Reference Types

Types from external modules aren't compiled by default. To include external types, you'll need to do two things:

##### 1. Modify your tsconfig to include the module's compiled types

```jsonc
// tsconfig.typedoc.json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    // ...
  },
  "include": ["./dist", "node_modules/<external-package-name>/dist"]
}
```

##### 2. Enable external module parsing in the typedoc configuration

```ts
// qui-typedoc.config.ts
import {BuildOptions} from "@qualcomm-ui/typedoc"

export default {
  // ...
  typedocOptions: {
    // this is `true` by default
    excludeExternals: false,
    tsconfig: "tsconfig.typedoc.json",
  },
} satisfies BuildOptions
```

## Recommendations and Known Issues

1. We recommend that you point typedoc at the compiled TypeScript types to improve compilation time. This is why we point our entryPoints at files in `dist`.
2. For Angular packages, the output types strip away necessary type information, so we target the package's src root instead, i.e. `./src/index.ts`.
3. Sometimes it is desirable to prevent the expansion of deeply nested types, like an interface that recursively references itself. We've enhanced the [@inheritDoc](https://typedoc.org/tags/inheritDoc/) tag for this purpose. Refer to the [JSDoc Tags](./#jsdoc-tags) section to learn more.

### Reference Types

**Ensure References are Exported for Full Expansion**

Type definitions (like interfaces or type aliases) used by exported members won't be fully expanded if they're not exported themselves. Consider this example:

```ts
interface InternalDefinition {
  /**
   * Some function
   */
  someFn: (args: string) => void
}

/**
 * @public
 */
export interface ExternalDefinition {
  /**
   * Property
   */
  property: InternalDefinition
}
```

- In this scenario, because `InternalDefinition` is not exported, the documentation generated for `ExternalDefinition.property` will only display the type name `InternalDefinition`.
- Our tool relies on TypeDoc's analysis of the public API, and unexported types are treated as internal implementation details. To ensure the detailed structure (e.g., `{ someFn: (args: string) => void }`) is shown, you must also export the `InternalDefinition` interface.

## JSDoc Tags

The following tags are enhanced with functionality in the UI.

### @default

Use the `@default` tag to indicate a default value for a property.

```ts
/**
 * @public
 */
export interface DefaultTagExample {
  /**
   * Example property.
   *
   * @default 0
   */
  age?: number
}
```

<TypeDocProps name="DefaultTagExample" />

### @inheritDoc

```ts
/**
 * @public
 */
export interface Option {
  /**
   * Unique identifier for the option.
   */
  id: string

  /**
   * Nested options.
   *
   * @inheritDoc
   */
  options?: Option[]

  /**
   * Option value.
   */
  value: string
}
```

<TypeDocProps name="Option" />

### @link

Context is applied conditionally to the inline `@link` tag.

- If the link starts with `https`, it's treated as an external link.
- If the tag refers to a named property, it's treated as an internal link.

```ts
/**
 * @public
 */
export interface LinkExample {
  /**
   * Visit {@link https://google.com this external link} to learn more.
   */
  externalLink?: string

  /**
   * Refer to the {@link externalLink} property.
   */
  internalLink?: string
}
```

<TypeDocProps name="LinkExample" />

### @option

Renders a bullet list entry for each option. Useful for documenting union or enum types.

```ts
export type WeightUnit = "kg" | "lb"

/**
 * @public
 */
export interface OptionTagExample {
  /**
   * The unit type of the weight field.
   *
   * @option `'kg'`: kilograms.
   * @option `'lb'`: pounds.
   */
  weightUnit: WeightUnit
}
```

<TypeDocProps partial name="OptionTagExample" />

### @see

Use the `@see` tag to render a separate section of documentation in the JSDoc comment. This is typically used to highlight related types or interfaces.

```ts
/**
 * @public
 */
export interface SeeTagExample {
  /**
   * @see {@link someOtherPropExample}
   */
  otherPropExample?: string

  /**
   * Another prop.
   */
  someOtherPropExample?: string
}
```

<TypeDocProps name="SeeTagExample" />

### @since

The `@since` tag is used to indicate when a property was added. The default configuration assumes that you have a changelog at `/changelog`, but this can be modified per instance of `TypeDocProps` using the `changelogPathname` prop:

```tsx
<TypeDocProps changelogPathname="/changelogs/mdx-docs" name="SinceExample" />
```

```ts
/**
 * @public
 */
export interface SinceExample {
  /**
   * Foo.
   *
   * @since 3.10.0
   */
  foo: string
}
```

<TypeDocProps
  changelogPathname="/changelogs/mdx-docs"
  name="SinceExample"
/>

## Typedoc Configuration

### Default Options

This module ships with reasonable defaults that enable efficient yet comprehensive TypeScript module documentation. You can override these defaults with the `typedocOptions` config property.

Refer to the corresponding [Typedoc documentation](https://typedoc.org/options/input/) for details about each property.

```ts
export const defaultOptions: Partial<TypeDocOptions> = {
  entryPointStrategy: "expand",
  // custom categories that we set to exclude specific properties or interfaces.
  excludeCategories: ["react-dom"],
  excludeExternals: true,
  excludeInternal: true,
  excludeNotDocumented: true,
  excludeNotDocumentedKinds: [
    "Module",
    "Namespace",
    "Enum",
    "Variable",
    "Function",
    "Class",
    "Constructor",
    "Property",
    "Method",
    "CallSignature",
    "IndexSignature",
    "ConstructorSignature",
    "Accessor",
    "GetSignature",
    "SetSignature",
    "Reference",
  ],
  excludePrivate: true,
  excludeProtected: true,
  logLevel: "Error",
  readme: "none",
}
```

# {frontmatter.title}

{frontmatter.description}

```typescript
import {Accordion} from "@qualcomm-ui/react/accordion"
```

## Usage

::: terms
a11y
:::

- The accordion requires each of its items to have a unique `value` input.
- The accordion is keyboard-navigable once focused. Arrow keys can be used to move to the next or previous item. Home and End keys can be used to jump to the first or last item, respectively.

## Examples

### Simple

Here's a typical usage example that uses the shorthand syntax for the item.

<Demo name="AccordionSimpleDemo" component={demos.AccordionSimpleDemo} />

### Composite

The following example is equivalent to the previous example, but uses the composite approach.

<Demo
  name="AccordionCompositeDemo"
  component={demos.AccordionCompositeDemo}
/>

### Composite Layout

::: terms
chevron position, arrow position, caret position
:::

Use the composite form only when the simple approach can't achieve your desired layout or behavior. The following example demonstrates how to display the expand/collapse indicator at the start of the trigger by changing its DOM position.

<Demo
  name="AccordionCompositeLayoutDemo"
  component={demos.AccordionCompositeLayoutDemo}
/>

### Multiple

::: terms
expand all, multi-expand, open several
:::

By default, only a single accordion section can be open at a time. Setting [multiple](./#multiple-1) allows multiple sections to be open or closed simultaneously.

<Demo
  name="AccordionMultipleDemo"
  component={demos.AccordionMultipleDemo}
/>

### Collapsible

::: terms
toggle closed, re-collapse
:::

When [multiple](./#multiple-1) is not set, enabling [collapsible](./#collapsible-1) lets the user close an open accordion item by clicking it again.

<Demo
  name="AccordionCollapsibleDemo"
  component={demos.AccordionCollapsibleDemo}
/>

### Default Value

::: terms
pre-expanded, start expanded
:::

The [defaultValue](./#defaultValue) prop allows you to set the initial state for the accordion by specifying which accordion item or items (if [multiple](./#multiple-1) is set) should be open by default.
It expects an array of values that should match those passed to each `Accordion.Item`.

<Demo
  name="AccordionDefaultValueDemo"
  component={demos.AccordionDefaultValueDemo}
/>

### Disabled

::: terms
inactive, greyed out, grayed out
:::

You can disable accordion items by setting their [disabled](./#disabled-2) prop. This prevents the item from being interacted with.
You can disable the entire accordion by setting the [disabled](./#disabled-1) prop on `Accordion.Root`.

<Demo
  name="AccordionDisabledDemo"
  component={demos.AccordionDisabledDemo}
/>

### Uncontained

::: terms
borderless, edge-to-edge
:::

Set the [uncontained](./#uncontained-1) prop when the accordion is not placed inside a container and needs to align flush with adjacent layout elements—such as when positioned directly below a paragraph of text.
This prop removes the default horizontal padding from accordion items, allowing them to sit seamlessly within the surrounding content.

<Demo
  name="AccordionUncontainedDemo"
  component={demos.AccordionUncontainedDemo}
/>

### Size

::: terms
small, medium, large
:::

Use the [size](./#size-1) prop to control the size of the accordion items. The available sizes are `sm`, `md` (default), and `lg`.

<Demo name="AccordionSizeDemo" component={demos.AccordionSizeDemo} />

### Secondary Text

::: terms
subtitle, helper text
:::

Use the `Accordion.ItemSecondaryText` component to display additional text opposite the trigger title.

<Demo
  name="AccordionSecondaryTextDemo"
  component={demos.AccordionSecondaryTextDemo}
/>

### Icon

::: terms
leading icon, prefix icon
:::

Pass an icon to the [icon](./#icon-1) prop on the `Accordion.ItemTrigger` element to display it next to the trigger title.

<Demo name="AccordionIconDemo" component={demos.AccordionIconDemo} />

> [!warning/UX considerations]
> In order to prevent visual confusion, only one icon can appear next to the trigger title. If you place the indicator at the start, the [icon prop](./#icon-1) will be ignored.

### Controlled State

::: terms
programmatic control
:::

The Accordion follows our [controlled state](/patterns/controlled-state) pattern with these three props:

- [value](./#value) - the controlled value that determines which accordion items are open.
- [onValueChange](./#onValueChange) - callback fired when the value changes: `(value: string[]) => void`
- [defaultValue](./#defaultValue) - initial state for uncontrolled mode

<Demo
  name="AccordionControlledStateDemo"
  component={demos.AccordionControlledStateDemo}
/>

::: terms
focus tracking
:::

The [onFocusChange](./#onFocusChange) prop allows you to listen for focus events on the accordion's items.

<Demo
  name="AccordionFocusCallbackDemo"

## Shortcuts

### Item Content

The `Accordion.ItemContent` component is a shortcut for the following:

```tsx
<AccordionItemContentAnimator>
  <AccordionItemContentBody>{children}</AccordionItemContentBody>
</AccordionItemContentAnimator>
```

### Item Shorthand

The `Accordion.Item` component is a shortcut for the following:

```tsx
<Accordion.ItemRoot>
  <Accordion.ItemTrigger>
    <Accordion.ItemText>{props.text}</Accordion.ItemText>
    {props.secondaryText ? (
      <Accordion.ItemSecondaryText>
        {props.secondaryText}
      </Accordion.ItemSecondaryText>
    ) : null}
    <Accordion.ItemIndicator />
  </Accordion.ItemTrigger>
  <Accordion.ItemContent>{props.children}</Accordion.ItemContent>
</Accordion.ItemRoot>
```

title: Avatar
description: Avatars provide visual representation of users, accounts, or entities. They support multiple content types including icons, initials, and images, with optional status indicators to communicate presence or state information.
component: Avatar
aliases: [profile picture, user photo, profile image]

import {TypeDocAttributes, TypeDocProps} from "@qualcomm-ui/react-mdx/typedoc"
import {ComponentExplorer, Demo} from "~components/demo"
import * as demos from "./demos"

# {frontmatter.title}

{frontmatter.description}

```typescript
import {Avatar} from "@qualcomm-ui/react/avatar"
```

## Usage

Avatars can display a user or entity image, initials, or custom content when an image is unavailable. They can also indicate the status of the user or entity.

## Overview

The anatomy of the avatar component is as follows:

- `Avatar.Root`: The main component.
- `Avatar.Image`: (optional) Displays an image as the avatar.
- `Avatar.Content`: (optional) Displays alternate content, such as initials or an icon, and acts as a fallback if the image fails to load..
- `Avatar.Status`: (optional) Shows a status indicator dot.

## Examples

### Showcase

Here's a typical usage example:

<Demo name="AvatarShowcaseDemo" component={demos.AvatarShowcaseDemo} />

### Content

::: terms
placeholder, broken image
:::

The `Avatar.Content` component displays alternative content within the avatar. Use it by itself to show a single character or an icon, or together with `Avatar.Image` to provide fallback content if the image cannot be loaded.

<Demo name="AvatarContentDemo" component={demos.AvatarContentDemo} />

### Sizes

::: terms
extra small, small, medium, large, extra large
:::

Use the [size](./#size) prop to set the size of the avatar. The available sizes are `xs`, `sm`, `md` (default), `lg`, and `xl`.

<Demo name="AvatarSizeDemo" component={demos.AvatarSizeDemo} />

### Emphasis

::: terms
high contrast, color scheme
:::

When displaying initials or an icon, use the [emphasis](./#emphasis-1) prop to set the avatar's color. Available values are `neutral` (default), `contrast`, and `brand`.

<Demo name="AvatarEmphasisDemo" component={demos.AvatarEmphasisDemo} />

### Status

::: terms
presence indicator, online
:::

To indicate the status of the user or entity, use the `Avatar.Status` component and set its [status](./#status-1) prop to one of: `active`, `offline` (default), `away`, or `busy`.

<Demo name="AvatarStatusDemo" component={demos.AvatarStatusDemo} />

### State Callback

::: terms
loading state, image loaded, image error
:::

You can listen for changes to the avatar's state by using the [onStateChange](./#onStateChange) prop.

<Demo
  expanded
  name="AvatarStateCallbackDemo"
  component={demos.AvatarStateCallbackDemo}
/>

# {frontmatter.title}

Source: https://github.com/qualcomm/qualcomm-ui/blob/main/packages/docs/react-docs/src/routes/components+/breadcrumbs+/_breadcrumbs.mdx

title: Breadcrumbs
description: Breadcrumbs help users understand their current location within a website or application hierarchy and provide a quick way to navigate back to parent pages.
component: Breadcrumbs
aliases: [breadcrumb trail, navigation path]

import {Demo} from "~components/demo"
import * as demos from "./demos"
import {TypeDocAttributes, TypeDocProps} from "@qualcomm-ui/react-mdx/typedoc"

# {frontmatter.title}

{frontmatter.description}

```tsx
import {Breadcrumbs} from "@qualcomm-ui/react/breadcrumbs"
```

## Overview

::: terms
a11y, WCAG, site hierarchy, wayfinding, location indicator
:::

- The root component should be labeled with `aria-label="Breadcrumbs"` to indicate that it's a breadcrumb navigation.
- The first breadcrumb item is always the root item, and is typically reserved for the home page or base route of your application.
- The last breadcrumb item represents the current page. Mark it with [`aria-current="page"`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-current).
- By default, `Breadcrumbs.Item` renders a `<span>` (non-link content). Pass the `render` prop when an item should navigate.

## Examples

### Links

::: terms
polymorphic, router, anchor
:::

[`Breadcrumbs.Item`](./#breadcrumbs-item) renders a non-link `<span>` by default, which is appropriate for the current page item. Use the [render](./#render-2) prop to make an item navigable. In most cases this will be your router's link component. Fall back to a plain `<a href>` if you don't use a router. The following example uses React Router:

<Demo name="BreadcrumbsLinksDemo" component={demos.BreadcrumbsLinksDemo} />

### Emphasis (color)

::: terms
neutral, muted, subdued
:::

Use the [emphasis](./#emphasis) prop to change the color of the breadcrumbs.

<Demo
  name="BreadcrumbsEmphasisDemo"
  component={demos.BreadcrumbsEmphasisDemo}
/>

### Sizes

::: terms
small, medium, large
:::

Three sizes are available via the [size](./#size) prop: `sm`, `md`, and `lg`. The default size is `md`.

<Demo name="BreadcrumbsSizesDemo" component={demos.BreadcrumbsSizesDemo} />

### Disabled Item

::: terms
inactive, non-clickable
:::

Use the [disabled](./#disabled) prop to disable a breadcrumb item.

<Demo
  name="BreadcrumbsDisabledDemo"
  component={demos.BreadcrumbsDisabledDemo}
/>

### Overflow

::: terms
overflow, collapsed, ellipsis, truncated
:::

Use the [`Breadcrumbs.OverflowItem`](./#breadcrumbs-overflow-item) component to collapse intermediate breadcrumb items into a [menu](/components/menu). The overflow trigger displays an ellipsis by default. Use the [icon](./#icon) prop to add an icon, or provide your own trigger via [`Breadcrumbs.OverflowTrigger`](./#breadcrumbs-overflow-trigger).

<Demo
  name="BreadcrumbsOverflowDemo"
  component={demos.BreadcrumbsOverflowDemo}
/>

### Tooltip

::: terms
tooltip, hover hint, title, description
:::

To provide additional context on hover, make [`Breadcrumbs.ItemTrigger`](./#breadcrumbs-item-trigger) a [Tooltip](/components/tooltip) trigger using the composite API.

<Demo
  name="BreadcrumbsTooltipDemo"
  component={demos.BreadcrumbsTooltipDemo}
/>

## Shortcuts

### Item

The [`Breadcrumbs.Item`](./#breadcrumbs-item) component is a convenient shorthand for rendering each part of the breadcrumb item. The trigger renders a `<span>` by default; pass the `render` prop to swap it for an anchor or a router link component.

```tsx
<Breadcrumbs.ItemRoot>
  <Breadcrumbs.ItemTrigger aria-current={ariaCurrent} render={render}>
    <Breadcrumbs.ItemIcon icon={icon} />
    {children}
  </Breadcrumbs.ItemTrigger>
  <Breadcrumbs.ItemSeparator />
</Breadcrumbs.ItemRoot>
```

### OverflowItem

The `Breadcrumbs.OverflowItem` component is a convenient shorthand that composes a menu trigger with the overflow ellipsis. It's equivalent to the following:

```tsx
<Breadcrumbs.OverflowItemRoot {...props}>
  <Menu.Root size={menuSize}>
    <Menu.Trigger>
      <Breadcrumbs.OverflowTrigger
        aria-label={ariaLabel}
        icon={icon}
        {...overflowTriggerProps}
      />
    </Menu.Trigger>
    <Portal>
      <Menu.Positioner>
        <Menu.Content>{children}</Menu.Content>
      </Menu.Positioner>
    </Portal>
  </Menu.Root>
  <Breadcrumbs.ItemSeparator icon={separator} {...separatorProps} />
</Breadcrumbs.OverflowItemRoot>
```

<Demo name="ButtonVariantsDemo" component={demos.ButtonVariantsDemo} />

### Contrast Colors

::: terms
high contrast button
button on dark background
inverted button
:::

Use `white-persistent` for buttons on dark backgrounds and `black-persistent` for buttons on light backgrounds. These emphasis values maintain consistent contrast regardless of the active theme.

<Demo name="ButtonContrastDemo" component={demos.ButtonContrastDemo} />

### Inverse Contrast

To flip contrast against the active theme, set [emphasis](./#emphasis) to `inverse`.

<Demo component={demos.ButtonInverseDemo} name="ButtonInverseDemo" />

### Menu Button

::: terms
menu trigger, dropdown button, icon menu button
:::

For a button that opens a dropdown, use [`Menu.Button`](/components/menu#menu-button) for a labeled trigger or [`Menu.IconButton`](/components/menu#menu-button) for an icon-only trigger.

### Split Button

::: terms
split action, dropdown button, secondary actions
:::

For a button that pairs a primary action with a dropdown of related actions, use [`Menu.SplitButton`](/components/menu#split-button).

# {frontmatter.title}

Source: https://github.com/qualcomm/qualcomm-ui/blob/main/packages/docs/react-docs/src/routes/components+/button-group+/_button-group.mdx

title: Button Group
description: Button groups organize related actions into a cohesive unit, reducing visual clutter while maintaining clear relationships between similar functions.
component: ButtonGroup
aliases: [button toolbar, action group, grouped buttons, button container]

import {TypeDocProps, TypeDocAttributes} from "@qualcomm-ui/react-mdx/typedoc"
import {Demo} from "~components/demo"
import * as demos from "./demos"

# {frontmatter.title}

{frontmatter.description}

```tsx
import {ButtonGroup} from "@qualcomm-ui/react/button"
```

## Usage

Use the `ButtonGroup` component to group related buttons together. This helps to visually associate buttons that perform similar actions.

## Examples

### Shared Props

::: terms
propagate
inherit
cascade
bulk apply
default props
:::

When you set certain props on the `ButtonGroup`, they are automatically applied to all child buttons. Some of these props can be overridden at the button level, while others cannot:

**Non-overridable:**

- [density](./#density), [disabled](./#disabled), and [size](./#size): if set on the group, all buttons will have the same corresponding property. The same prop on individual buttons will be ignored.

**Overridable:**

- [emphasis](./#emphasis) and [variant](./#variant): If set on the group, these will be the default for all buttons, but individual buttons can override them as needed.

<Demo
  name="ButtonGroupSharedPropsDemo"
  component={demos.ButtonGroupSharedPropsDemo}
/>

### Layout

::: terms
button alignment
justify buttons
:::

Use the [layout](./#layout-1) prop to control how the button group is sized and aligned within its container. Options include:

- `hug`: Content-sized; width matches the buttons only (default).
- `start`: Full width; buttons are aligned to the start edge.
- `end`: Full width; buttons are aligned to the end edge.
- `fill`: Full width; buttons share space evenly.

Borders have been added to the example below to better illustrate these layout options.

<Demo
  name="ButtonGroupLayoutDemo"
  component={demos.ButtonGroupLayoutDemo}
/>

## Accessibility

::: terms
screen reader
a11y
:::

You should provide a meaningful label for the button group using either the `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` prop.

## API

### \<ButtonGroup>

<TypeDocProps name="ButtonGroupProps" />

<TypeDocAttributes name={["QdsButtonGroupBindings"]} />

  name="CheckboxCompositeLayoutDemo"

/>

### States

Based on the inputs, the checkbox will render as checked, indeterminate, or unchecked (default). The checked state takes precedence over indeterminate.

::: spoiler State Table

| checked | indeterminate | Result State                                                     |
| ------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `false` | `false`       | <Checkbox label="unchecked" checked={false} />                   |
| `false` | `true`        | <Checkbox label="indeterminate" indeterminate checked={false} /> |
| `true`  | `false`       | <Checkbox label="checked" checked />                             |
| `true`  | `true`        | <Checkbox label="checked" indeterminate checked />               |

:::

<Demo name="CheckboxStatesDemo" component={demos.CheckboxStatesDemo} />

### Disabled State

When [disabled](./#disabled) is true, the checkbox becomes non-interactive and is typically rendered with reduced opacity to indicate its unavailable state.

<Demo name="CheckboxDisabledDemo" component={demos.CheckboxDisabledDemo} />

### Controlled State

::: terms
uncontrolled
:::

Set the initial value using the [defaultChecked](./#defaultChecked) prop, or use [checked](./#checked) and [onCheckedChange](./#onCheckedChange) to control the value manually. These props follow our [controlled state](/patterns/controlled-state) pattern.

<Demo
  expanded
  name="CheckboxControlledDemo"
  component={demos.CheckboxControlledDemo}
/>

### Sizes

::: terms
small
medium
large
:::

Checkboxes come in three sizes: `sm`, `md`, and `lg`. The default size is `md`.

<Demo
  expanded
  name="CheckboxSizesDemo"
  component={demos.CheckboxSizesDemo}
/>

::: terms
helper text
description
:::

<Demo name="CheckboxHintDemo" component={demos.CheckboxHintDemo} />

### Group

::: terms
checkbox group
field group
:::

Use [CheckboxGroup](/components/checkbox-group) to group related checkboxes with a shared label, hint text, and validation state.

## Forms

## Composite Guidelines

The composite elements are only intended to be used as direct descendants of the `<Checkbox.Root>` component.

```tsx
/* Won't work alone ❌ */
<Checkbox.HiddenInput />
<Checkbox.Control />

/* Works as expected ✅ */
<Checkbox.Root>
  <Checkbox.HiddenInput />
  <Checkbox.Control />
</Checkbox.Root>
```

## Overview

```tsx
      </Combobox.Item>
    )
  }}
/>
```

### States

::: terms
disabled combobox, read only, readonly
:::

The following shows how the Combobox component appears in each interactive state.

<Demo name="ComboboxStatesDemo" component={demos.ComboboxStatesDemo} />

### Error Text and Indicator

::: terms
validation, form error
:::

Error messages are displayed using two props:

- [invalid](./#invalid)
- [errorText](./#errorText) (or the `Combobox.ErrorText` component when using the composite API)

The error text and indicator will only render when [invalid](./#invalid) is true.

<Demo name="ComboboxErrorDemo" component={demos.ComboboxErrorDemo} />

### Hint Text

::: terms
helper text, description text
:::

Use the [hint](./#hint) prop to provide additional context or instructions below the combobox.

<Demo name="ComboboxHintDemo" component={demos.ComboboxHintDemo} />

### Within Dialog

::: terms
modal, nested combobox, portalProps.disabled
:::

To use the Combobox within a [Dialog](/components/dialog), you need to avoid portalling the `Combobox.Positioner` to the document's body. To do this using the simple API, set `portalProps.disabled` to `true`:

<Demo
  name="ComboboxWithinDialogDemo"
  component={demos.ComboboxWithinDialogDemo}
/>

### Within Popover

::: terms
portal disabled
:::

Like with the [Dialog](/components/dialog), you need to avoid portalling the `Combobox.Positioner` to the document's body:

<Demo
  name="ComboboxWithinPopoverDemo"
  component={demos.ComboboxWithinPopoverDemo}

::: terms
remote data, fetch, api data, server-side data
:::

This example shows how to load items asynchronously and display a loading indicator.

<Demo name="ComboboxAsyncDemo" component={demos.ComboboxAsyncDemo} />

### Virtualized

::: terms
windowing, virtual scrolling
:::

For large lists, use the [virtual](./#virtual) prop to improve performance. This virtualizes the visible list items for performant scrolling and searching. The following example features a list of 5000 mock usernames.

<Demo name="ComboboxVirtualDemo" component={demos.ComboboxVirtualDemo} />

## Data Structures

### ListCollection

The following describes the member variables and methods of the `ListCollection` class. The Combobox component uses an instance of this class as input:

```tsx
const collection = comboboxCollection({
  items: [
    // ...
  ],
})

return <Combobox collection={collection} />
```

Note that the ListCollection accepts a single generic type parameter, `T`, which is the type of each list item used in the collection. This can be a string or an object.

show

programmatic

### Outside Scroll

::: terms
overflow
page scroll

::: terms
confirmation

delete
destructive
:::

This is recommended for situations where the dialog is used to notify users of urgent information that demands their immediate attention.

<Demo
  name="DialogAlertDialogDemo"

/>

## Shortcuts

### \<Dialog.FloatingPortal>

A helper component that combines the portal, positioner, and content
components. This shortcut is equivalent to:

```tsx
<Portal {...props}>
  <Dialog.Backdrop {...backdropProps} />
  <Dialog.Positioner {...positionerProps}>
    <Dialog.Content {...contentProps}>{children}</Dialog.Content>
  </Dialog.Positioner>
</Portal>
```

```typescript
import {Divider} from "@qualcomm-ui/react/divider"
```

## Examples

### Showcase

::: terms
content separator, section break, visual separation
:::

A horizontal line separating two blocks of content.

<Demo name="DividerShowcaseDemo" component={demos.DividerShowcaseDemo} />

### Variants

::: terms
subtle, normal, strong, low contrast, high contrast, visual weight
:::

Use [variant](./#variant) to change the visual emphasis level of the divider.

<Demo name="DividerVariantsDemo" component={demos.DividerVariantsDemo} />

### Orientation

::: terms
column divider, inline separator, row divider
:::

By default, a divider has a `horizontal` orientation. You can change this by setting the [orientation](./#orientation) prop to `vertical`.

<Demo
  name="DividerOrientationDemo"
  component={demos.DividerOrientationDemo}
/>

### Focusable

::: terms
keyboard navigation, tab order, screen reader, a11y
:::

By default, a divider is not focusable. You can change this by setting a `tabindex` value. Authors can assign `aria-label` to provide accessible names to dividers.

A focusable divider [must expose a value to accessibility tools](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#separator). Authors must set the "aria-valuenow" attribute.

<Demo name="DividerFocusableDemo" component={demos.DividerFocusableDemo} />

### Value Text

::: terms
aria-valuetext, accessible value, assistive technology
:::

When the value itself is not sufficient to describe the state of the component, authors can provide a more descriptive text using the `valueText` prop.

<Demo name="DividerValueTextDemo" component={demos.DividerValueTextDemo} />

embedded drawer
inline drawer
nested drawer
contained drawer
non-fullscreen drawer

Size can be customized using the [size](./#size) input. There are five available values: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`. Should you need more control over the rendered size, supply a number instead which will be converted to pixels.

<Demo name="IconSizesDemo" component={demos.IconSizesDemo} />

## Accessibility Guidelines

::: terms
a11y
wcag
:::

Icon-only buttons rely on visual cues that screen readers cannot access. Use [aria-label](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-label) or [aria-labelledby](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-labelledby) to give every icon-only button an accessible name so its purpose is clear to assistive technologies.

```tsx
import {Menu} from "@qualcomm-ui/react/menu"
```

## Examples

### Item Customization

::: terms
hotkeys, keyboard shortcuts, action list, overflow menu
:::

Compose the menu to include icons and commands.

<Demo
  name="MenuItemCustomizationDemo"
  component={demos.MenuItemCustomizationDemo}
/>

### Menu Button

::: terms
menu trigger, dropdown button, icon menu button
:::

Use [`<Menu.Button>`](./#menu-button-1) for a labeled trigger and [`<Menu.IconButton>`](./#menu-icon-button) for an icon-only trigger. Both automatically render a chevron indicator. Always provide an [`aria-label`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-label) on `<Menu.IconButton>` to give assistive technologies an accessible name. Control the menu position with [positioning.placement](./#positioning).

<Demo name="MenuButtonDemo" component={demos.MenuButtonDemo} />

### Split Button

::: terms
split action, dropdown button, secondary actions
:::

Use [`<Menu.SplitButton>`](./#menu-split-button) for a split button trigger. The icon-only trigger provides a default "More options" `aria-label`; use [`triggerProps`](./#triggerProps) to override it. Optionally add an `aria-label` on the group when both halves share an accessible name. Control the menu position with [positioning.placement](./#positioning) on the parent [`<Menu.Root>`](./#menu-root).

<Demo name="MenuSplitButtonDemo" component={demos.MenuSplitButtonDemo} />

### Context Menu

::: terms

### Links

::: terms
anchor, navigation, navigation menu
:::

Menu items can be links using [polymorphic composition](/polymorphic-components). Use the [render](./#render) prop on the `<Menu.Item>` to specify the element type.

<Demo name="MenuLinksDemo" component={demos.MenuLinksDemo} />

### Groups

Use the [`<Menu.ItemGroup>`](./#menu-item-group) component to group menu items.

### Item Types

There are three item types, each corresponding to one of the three types of aria menu item roles:

- `<Menu.Item>` — `menuitem`
- `<Menu.RadioItem>` — `menuitemradio`
- `<Menu.CheckboxItem>` — `menuitemcheckbox`

#### Checkbox Items

::: terms
multi-select, toggle
:::

There are two appearance options:

- For a checkbox appearance, render the [`<Menu.CheckboxItemControl>`](./#menu-checkbox-item-control) element as a child of the item.
- Render the [`<Menu.ItemIndicator />`](./#menu-item-indicator) element for a simple selection indicator.

<Demo
  name="MenuCheckboxItemsDemo"
  component={demos.MenuCheckboxItemsDemo}
/>

#### Checkbox Selection State

::: terms
onCheckedChange, controlled checkbox
:::

Illustrates how to manage and reflect the checked state of checkbox menu items.

<Demo
  name="MenuCheckboxSelectionStateDemo"
  component={demos.MenuCheckboxSelectionStateDemo}
/>

#### Radio Group

::: terms
single-select, exclusive selection
:::

Demonstrates how to group radio menu items so only one can be selected at a time.

<Demo name="MenuRadioGroupDemo" component={demos.MenuRadioGroupDemo} />

### Controlled State

The menu's visibility can be controlled via the [`open`](./#open), [`onOpenChange`](./#onOpenChange), and [`defaultOpen`](./#defaultOpen) props.

- Use `open` to explicitly set whether the menu is open (controlled mode).
- Use `onOpenChange` to be notified when the menu requests to open or close.
- Use `defaultOpen` to set the initial open state when you don't need to control it yourself (uncontrolled mode).

In controlled mode, the `open` prop should be updated in response to `onOpenChange` events to reflect the desired visibility.

<Demo
  name="MenuControlledStateDemo"
  component={demos.MenuControlledStateDemo}
/>

### Placement

::: terms
position, popover placement
:::

Configure the menu's placement using the [positioning.placement](./#positioning) prop.

<Demo name="MenuPlacementDemo" component={demos.MenuPlacementDemo} />

### Sizes

::: terms
small, medium
:::

Use the [size](./#size) prop on `<Menu.Root>` to control the size of the menu. The default size is `md`. The demo features the small (`sm`) size.

The `<Menu.Button>` and `<Menu.IconButton>` triggers inherit the menu's size, so the trigger and menu match by default. Such a trigger can run larger than its menu: set [size](./#size) on it to override the inherited value. An `md` menu pairs with an `md` or `lg` trigger. A compact trigger should always pair with an `sm` menu. When a trigger uses `density="compact"`, set `size="sm"` on `<Menu.Root>`.

Other trigger content does not inherit the menu size. A link, an avatar, or a custom element placed in the trigger must be sized directly.

<Demo name="MenuSizesDemo" component={demos.MenuSizesDemo} />

### Anchor Point

::: terms
getAnchorRect, custom anchor
:::

Use the [positioning.anchorPoint](./#positioning) prop to control the anchor point of the menu.

<Demo name="MenuAnchorPointDemo" component={demos.MenuAnchorPointDemo} />

### Avatar

::: terms
profile menu, user menu, account dropdown
:::

Here's an example that composes the `Menu` with the [Avatar](/components/avatar) component to display a user account menu.

<Demo name="MenuAvatarDemo" component={demos.MenuAvatarDemo} />

### Within Dialog

::: terms
modal, overlay composition
:::

When using the `Menu` inside a [Dialog](/components/dialog), don't render the `<Menu.Positioner>` within a `<Portal>` element.

<Demo name="MenuWithinDialogDemo" component={demos.MenuWithinDialogDemo} />

### Hide When Detached

::: terms
auto-hide, scroll behavior, overflow
:::

Use the [positioning.hideWhenDetached](./#positioning) prop to hide the menu when it's detached from the trigger.

<Demo
  name="MenuHideWhenDetachedDemo"
  component={demos.MenuHideWhenDetachedDemo}
/>

### Ranges

  expanded
  name="PaginationRangesDemo"
  component={demos.PaginationRangesDemo}
/>

### Controlled State

The Pagination component follows our [controlled state](/patterns/controlled-state) pattern for its [page](./#page) and [pageSize](./#pageSize) props.

By default, the component is uncontrolled and manages these values internally. You may optionally control the current page or page size by supplying the properties and their corresponding onChange functions:

<Demo
  expanded
  name="PaginationControlledStateDemo"
  component={demos.PaginationControlledStateDemo}
/>

## Shortcuts

Shortcuts enable quick implementations for common use cases.

### PageItems

Rendering `<Pagination.PageItems />` is shorthand for this:

```tsx
<PaginationContext>
  {(context) => (
    <>
      {context.pageItems.map((item, index) => {
        const itemProps = context.getPageItemProps(item)
        return <Pagination.PageItem key={index} {...itemProps} />
      })}
      {children}
    </>
  )}
</PaginationContext>
```

### PageSize

The `<Pagination.PageSize />` shortcut is a convenient dropdown for selecting the number of items per page. It's shorthand for this:

```tsx
<PolymorphicElement as="div" {...mergedProps}>
  {children}
  <Menu.Root
    onSelect={(value) => {
      setPageSize(parseInt(value))
    }}
    size={qdsContext.size}
  >
    <Menu.Trigger>
      <Menu.Button
        aria-labelledby={pageSizeLabelId}
        emphasis="neutral"
        size={qdsContext.size}
        variant="outline"
      >
        {pageSize}
      </Menu.Button>
    </Menu.Trigger>
    <Portal>
      <Menu.Positioner>
        <Menu.Content>
          {options.map((opt) => (
            <Menu.Item key={opt} value={`${opt}`}>
              {opt}
            </Menu.Item>
          ))}
        </Menu.Content>
      </Menu.Positioner>
    </Portal>
  </Menu.Root>
</PolymorphicElement>
```

### PageButtons

The `<Pagination.PageButtons>` shortcut renders the prev, next, and individual page buttons:

```tsx
<ActionGroup {...props}>
  <Pagination.PrevTrigger />
  <Pagination.PageItems />
  <Pagination.NextTrigger />
</ActionGroup>
```

component: Popover
aliases: [popup, floating panel, flyout, callout, bubble]

import {TypeDocAttributes, TypeDocProps} from "@qualcomm-ui/react-mdx/typedoc"
import {ComponentExplorer, Demo} from "~components/demo"
import * as demos from "./demos"


## Examples

### Simple

Basic popover using the simple API with a label and child content.

<Demo name="PopoverSimpleDemo" component={demos.PopoverSimpleDemo} />

### Composite

::: terms
arrow, portal, anchor, positioner
:::

Build with the composite API for granular control. This API requires you to provide each subcomponent, but gives you full control over the structure and layout.

<Demo name="PopoverCompositeDemo" component={demos.PopoverCompositeDemo} />

<Demo name="PopoverEmphasisDemo" component={demos.PopoverEmphasisDemo} />

## Accessibility

::: terms
a11y
:::

- The anchor element is automatically associated with the popover:
- When the popover is visible, the anchor element receives the [`aria-controls`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-controls) and [`aria-expanded`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-expanded) attributes.
- The anchor element's [`aria-haspopup`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-haspopup) is always set to `'true'`.
- When the [`Popover.Label`](./#popover-label) component is supplied, the overlay panel's [`aria-labelledby`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-labelledby) attribute is set to the id of the label.
- When the [`Popover.Description`](./#popover-description) component is supplied, the overlay panel's [`aria-describedby`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-describedby) attribute is set to the id of the label.

> [!note]
> Don't worry about supplying id's to the label, description or popover. If these aren't provided, they'll be generated automatically.

# {frontmatter.title}

Source: https://github.com/qualcomm/qualcomm-ui/blob/main/packages/docs/react-docs/src/routes/components+/progress+/_progress.mdx

title: Progress
description: Progress bars provide clear visual feedback about task completion or loading states, helping users understand system status and perceived remaining time.
component: Progress
aliases: [progress bar, loading bar]

import {ComponentExplorer, Demo} from "~components/demo"
import * as demos from "./demos"
import {TypeDocAttributes, TypeDocProps} from "@qualcomm-ui/react-mdx/typedoc"

# {frontmatter.title}

{frontmatter.description}

```tsx
import {Progress} from "@qualcomm-ui/react/progress"
```

## Overview

The progress ring can be in one of two states:

- indeterminate: the default state.
- determinate: assumed when the [value](./#value) prop is passed.

Indeterminate progress bars keep users informed that work is happening when timeframes are unknown.

## Examples

### Simple

The simple API provides a standalone component with built-in layout.

<Demo name="ProgressSimpleDemo" component={demos.ProgressSimpleDemo} />

### Composite

Build with the composite API for granular control. This API requires you to provide each subcomponent, but gives you full control over the structure and layout.

<Demo
  name="ProgressCompositeDemo"
  component={demos.ProgressCompositeDemo}
/>

### Label Orientation

Use the [labelOrientation](./#labelOrientation) property to change the positioning of the label and value text relative to the progress bar.

<Demo
  name="ProgressLabelOrientationDemo"
  component={demos.ProgressLabelOrientationDemo}
/>

### Sizes

::: terms
small, medium, large
:::

Progress bars support three sizes: `sm`, `md`, and `lg`.

<Demo name="ProgressSizeDemo" component={demos.ProgressSizeDemo} />

### Emphasis (Color)

Set the color of the progress bar using the [emphasis](./#emphasis) property. The available options are `primary` and `neutral`.

<Demo name="ProgressEmphasisDemo" component={demos.ProgressEmphasisDemo} />

### Disabled

Use the [disabled](./#disabled-1) prop to indicate that the progress indicator is inactive.

<Demo name="ProgressDisabledDemo" component={demos.ProgressDisabledDemo} />

### Error Text

Error messages are displayed using two props:

- [invalid](./#invalid)
- [errorText](./#errorText) (or the `Progress.ErrorText` component when using the composite API)

The error text will only render when `invalid` is true.

<Demo
  name="ProgressErrorTextDemo"
  component={demos.ProgressErrorTextDemo}
/>

## Shortcuts

### Track and Bar

The `Progress.Track` automatically renders a `Progress.Bar` when no children as passed to it.

```tsx
<Progress.Track />
```

is equivalent to

```tsx
<Progress.Track>
  <Progress.Bar />
</Progress.Track>
```

## Accessibility

::: terms
a11y, screen reader, wcag
:::

- When the value is supplied, the component automatically provides the corresponding `aria-value*` attributes to the element.
- The progress element is automatically marked with [`role="progressbar"`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Roles).
- The [label](./#label) is automatically associated with the progress bar. If you omit the [label](./#label) property, the [`aria-label`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-label) of the progress element defaults to the [value](./#value) when determinate, and "Loading" when indeterminate.

## Shortcuts

The `ProgressRing.Circle` component automatically renders the track and bar components when child. The following two examples are

```tsx
<ProgressRing.Circle />
```

## Accessibility

::: terms
a11y
:::

- When the value is supplied, the component automatically provides the corresponding `aria-value*` attributes to the element.
- The progress element is automatically marked with [`role="progressbar"`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Roles).
- The [label](./#label) is automatically associated with the progress bar. If you omit the [label](./#label) property, the [`aria-label`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-label) of the progress element defaults to the [value](./#value) when determinate, and "Loading" when indeterminate.

## Guidelines

### RadioGroup

The Radio is only intended to be used as direct descendants of the `<RadioGroup.Root>` component.

```tsx
/* Won't work alone ❌ */
<Radio label="Label" value="value" />

/* Works as expected ✅ */
<RadioGroup.Root>
  <Radio label="Label" value="value" />
</RadioGroup.Root>
```

### Composite Components

The Radio's composite components are only intended to be used as direct descendants of the `<Radio.Root>` component.

```tsx
/* Won't work alone ❌ */
<Radio.HiddenInput />
<Radio.Control />

/* Works as expected ✅ */
<Radio.Root>
  <Radio.HiddenInput />
  <Radio.Control />
</Radio.Root>
```

# {frontmatter.title}

{frontmatter.description}

```tsx
import {SegmentedControl} from "@qualcomm-ui/react/segmented-control"
```

## Usage

The `SegmentedControl` component allows users to make a selection from multiple options, exclusive (similar to radio buttons) or not (similar to checkboxes).
It is typically used for filtering content, sorting elements or switching between views within the same context.

## Examples

### Simple

::: terms
basic example
getting started
:::

::: terms
subcomponents
custom structure

:::

  name="SegmentedControlCompositeDemo"
  component={demos.SegmentedControlCompositeDemo}
/>

### Multiple

::: terms
multi-select
checkbox-like
multiple selection
:::

By default, a segmented control allows for a single selection. Use the [multiple](./#multiple-1) prop to create a segmented control that allows for multiple selections.

<Demo
  name="SegmentedControlMultipleDemo"
  component={demos.SegmentedControlMultipleDemo}
/>

### Orientation

Use the [orientation](./#orientation-1) prop to control the layout direction of the `SegmentedControl`. Options include:

- `horizontal`: Items are laid out in a row (default).
- `vertical`: Items are laid out in a column.

<Demo
  name="SegmentedControlOrientationDemo"
  component={demos.SegmentedControlOrientationDemo}
/>

### Icon

<Demo
  name="SegmentedControlIconDemo"
  component={demos.SegmentedControlIconDemo}
/>

### Layout

Use the [layout](./#layout-1) prop to control how the `SegmentedControl` is sized and aligned within its container. Options include:

- `hug`: Content-sized; width matches the items only (default).
- `fill`: Full width; items share space evenly.

<Demo
  name="SegmentedControlLayoutDemo"
  component={demos.SegmentedControlLayoutDemo}

::: terms
small

:::

## Accessibility

### Keyboard Navigation

::: terms
keyboard shortcuts
keyboard support
focus management
:::

Users can navigate the segmented control using the keyboard. The following keys are supported:

- `Tab`/`Shift + Tab`: Move focus between items.
- `Space`/`Enter`: Select the focused item. Unselects an already selected item if [multiple](./#multiple-1) is set.

### Icon only

::: terms

a11y
:::

While it is possible to use icon-only items in the segmented control, it is important to ensure that they are easily understood and accessible.

The following describes the member variables and methods of the `ListCollection` class. The Select component uses an instance of this class as input:

```tsx
const collection = selectCollection({

    // ...
  ],
})

return <Select collection={collection} />
```

Note that the ListCollection accepts a single generic type parameter, `T`, which is the type of each list item used in the collection. This can be a string or an object.

# {frontmatter.title}

Source: https://github.com/qualcomm/qualcomm-ui/blob/main/packages/docs/react-docs/src/routes/components+/side-nav+/_side-nav.mdx

title: Side Nav
description: The side navigation provides a consistent, easy-to-scan way for users to move through major sections of an application. It stays visible as users browse, giving them a clear understanding of where they are and what options are available.
component: SideNav
aliases: [sidebar, left nav, navigation menu, vertical menu]

import {Demo} from "~components/demo"
import * as demos from "./demos"
import {TypeDocAttributes, TypeDocProps} from "@qualcomm-ui/react-mdx/typedoc"

# {frontmatter.title}

{frontmatter.description}

```tsx
import {SideNav} from "@qualcomm-ui/react/side-nav"
```

## Overview

The side nav is an extension of our [tree](/components/tree) component.

- The Side Navigation relies on the `TreeCollection` class to manage its items. Refer to the [API](./#tree-collection) below for details.
- Like with the tree, Side Navigations are composed of nodes, which are objects that describe the navigation SideNav. There are two types of nodes:
- A `branch` node has children.
- A `leaf` node does not have any children.
- Each node has a `value` (unique identifier used for expansion) and a `text` (display text).

**Default object shape:**

- `value` (required): unique identifier for expansion/selection
- `text` (required): display text
- `nodes` (optional): child nodes for branches
- `disabled` (optional): prevents interaction when `true`

These keys can be customized via the `TreeCollection` [constructor](./#constructor).

## Examples

### Node Shorthand

We expose the `<SideNav.Nodes>` shorthand for rendering nodes. Use its [renderBranch](./#renderBranch) and [renderLeaf](./#renderLeaf) render props to customize the content of each tree node.

Note that `<SideNav.Nodes>` automatically renders child nodes for branches, so you only have to customize the content of the node itself.

<Demo
  name="SideNavNodeShorthandDemo"
  component={demos.SideNavNodeShorthandDemo}
/>

### Grouping

::: terms
section divider, categorize items, navigation sections
:::

Group nodes using the collection's [groupChildren](./#groupChildren) method. This should be called on the top-level node of your SideNav. Nested groups are not supported.

<Demo name="SideNavGroupsDemo" component={demos.SideNavGroupsDemo} />

### Default Expanded

::: terms
initially open, pre-expanded
:::

Expand nodes by default using the [defaultExpandedValue](./#defaultExpandedValue) prop. Or use [expandedValue](./#expandedValue) and [onExpandedValueChange](./#onExpandedValueChange) to control the expansion manually. These props follow our [controlled state](/patterns/controlled-state) pattern.

<Demo
  name="SideNavDefaultExpandedDemo"
  component={demos.SideNavDefaultExpandedDemo}
/>

### Disabled Nodes

::: terms
inactive, unavailable
:::

You can disable nodes by setting the `disabled` property on the node object.

<Demo
  name="SideNavDisabledNodeDemo"
  component={demos.SideNavDisabledNodeDemo}
/>

### Filtering

::: terms
fuzzy search, SideNav.FilterInput
:::

Here's an example that filters the items using `matchSorter`.

<Demo name="SideNavFilteringDemo" component={demos.SideNavFilteringDemo} />

### Links

::: terms
react-router, router integration
:::

Side Nav nodes can be links using [polymorphic composition](/polymorphic-components). Use the `render` prop on the `<SideNav.LeafNode>` to specify the element type.

<Demo name="SideNavLinksDemo" component={demos.SideNavLinksDemo} />

### Collapsed

::: terms
minimize, icon-only, compact, hamburger, drawer menu
:::

Side Nav can be collapsed to render only the top-level icons.

The open state of the panel can be controlled using the [open](./#open), [onOpenChange](./#onOpenChange) and [defaultOpen](./#defaultOpen) props. These props follow our [controlled state](/patterns/controlled-state) pattern.

<Demo name="SideNavCollapsedDemo" component={demos.SideNavCollapsedDemo} />

### Tooltips

::: terms
hover hints, icon labels
:::

Consider wrapping collapsed nodes with the [Tooltip](/components/tooltip) component to provide context about each item. This is also useful for describing disabled nodes.

<Demo name="SideNavTooltipDemo" component={demos.SideNavTooltipDemo} />

# {frontmatter.title}

Source: https://github.com/qualcomm/qualcomm-ui/blob/main/packages/docs/react-docs/src/routes/components+/slider+/_slider.mdx

title: Slider
description: A slider is an input control that allows users to adjust a single value or a value range along a defined linear scale. It provides a draggable handle mapped to a continuous or discrete interval.
component: Slider
aliases: [range slider, range picker]

import {TypeDocAttributes, TypeDocProps} from "@qualcomm-ui/react-mdx/typedoc"
import {Slider} from "@qualcomm-ui/react/slider"
import {ComponentExplorer, Demo} from "~components/demo"
import * as demos from "./demos"

# {frontmatter.title}

{frontmatter.description}

```typescript
import {Slider} from "@qualcomm-ui/react/slider"
```

## Usage

::: terms
input control
:::

Sliders allow users to select a value or range from a continuous or discrete set by moving an indicator (thumb) along a track. They are best used for settings that reflect a range of values rather than precise input.

## Examples

### Simple

Use the simple API to create a slider using minimal markup.

<Demo name="SliderSimpleDemo" component={demos.SliderSimpleDemo} />

### Composite

Build with the composite API for granular control. This API requires you to provide each subcomponent, but gives you full control over the structure and layout.

<Demo name="SliderCompositeDemo" component={demos.SliderCompositeDemo} />

### Min/Max/Step

::: terms
scale, interval
:::

The [min](./#min), [max](./#max), and [step](./#step) props control the slider's value range and increments:

- `min`: The minimum value of the slider (default is 0).
- `max`: The maximum value of the slider (default is 100).
- `step`: The increment/decrement step value (default is 1).

<Demo name="SliderMinMaxStepDemo" component={demos.SliderMinMaxStepDemo} />

### Origin

::: terms
fill direction
:::

Use [origin](./#origin) to control where the track is filled from for single-value sliders:

- `start`: Fills from the start of the track to the thumb. Useful when the value represents an absolute value (default).
- `center`: Fills from the center of the track to the thumb. Useful when the value represents an offset or relative value.
- `end`: Fills from the end of the track to the thumb. Useful when the value represents an offset from the end.

<Demo name="SliderOriginDemo" component={demos.SliderOriginDemo} />

### Tooltip

::: terms
value indicator
thumb label
:::

Use the [tooltip](./#tooltip-1) prop to display the slider's value in a tooltip rather than above the component.

<Demo name="SliderTooltipDemo" component={demos.SliderTooltipDemo} />

#### Display

You can customize the tooltip's content by using the [composite API](./#thumbs-with-tooltips) and passing a function to [display](./#display-3) on the `SliderThumbIndicator` component.

<Demo
  name="SliderTooltipDisplayDemo"
  component={demos.SliderTooltipDisplayDemo}
/>

### Markers

#### Track Markers

::: terms
tick marks
:::

By default, the component generates 11 marks based on the slider's [min](./#min) and [max](./#max) values.
provide your own set of marks by passing them in an array to the [marks](./#marks) prop.

<Demo name="SliderMarkersDemo" component={demos.SliderMarkersDemo} />

#### Side Markers

::: terms
endpoint labels
:::

For more compact designs, you can display the `min` and `max` markers at the ends of the track using the [sideMarkers](./#sideMarkers) prop.

<Demo
  name="SliderSideMarkersDemo"
  component={demos.SliderSideMarkersDemo}
/>

### Range

::: terms
dual thumb, two handles
:::

Set the [value](./#value) or [defaultValue](./#defaultValue) prop with two values to create a range slider.

<Demo name="SliderRangeDemo" component={demos.SliderRangeDemo} />

#### Minimum Steps Between Thumbs

::: terms
thumb collision
:::

To prevent overlapping thumbs, you can use the [minStepsBetweenThumbs](./#minStepsBetweenThumbs) prop to set a minimum distance between them.

<Demo name="SliderMinStepsDemo" component={demos.SliderMinStepsDemo} />

#### Display

By default, range values are displayed separated by a dash (-). You can customize this by passing a separator string or a function to the [display](./#display-1) prop.

<Demo name="SliderDisplayDemo" component={demos.SliderDisplayDemo} />

### Size

Set the [size](./#size-1) prop to adjust the size of the thumbs. Available sizes are `sm` (small) and `md` (medium, default).

<Demo name="SliderSizeDemo" component={demos.SliderSizeDemo} />

### Variant

Set the [variant](./#variant-1) prop to adjust the visual style of the slider. Available variants are `neutral` and `primary` (default).

<Demo name="SliderVariantDemo" component={demos.SliderVariantDemo} />

### Hint

Use the [hint](./#hint-1) prop to add additional guidance or context to the user below the slider.

<Demo name="SliderHintDemo" component={demos.SliderHintDemo} />

### Disabled

Use the [disabled](./#disabled-1) prop to prevent user interaction.

<Demo name="SliderDisabledDemo" component={demos.SliderDisabledDemo} />

### Focus Callback

The [onFocusChange](./#onFocusChange) prop allows you to listen for focus events on the slider's thumbs.

<Demo
  name="SliderFocusCallbackDemo"
  component={demos.SliderFocusCallbackDemo}
/>

### Controlled State

Use [value](./#value) and [onValueChange](./#onValueChange) or [onValueChangeEnd](./#onValueChangeEnd) to control the value of the slider. This allows for more complex interactions and integration with form libraries.

<Demo
  name="SliderValueCallbackDemo"
  component={demos.SliderValueCallbackDemo}
/>

## Composite API and Shortcuts

The Slider component provides a composite API should you need more control over the slider's behavior and appearance.

### Anatomy

::: terms
drag, handle, thumb
:::

The composite API is based on the following components:

- `Slider.Root`: The main component that wraps the slider subcomponents.
- `Slider.Label`: The slider main label.
- `Slider.ValueText`: The slider current value as text.
- `Slider.Control`: The container for the thumb(s) and its track and range.
- `Slider.Track`: The track along which the thumb(s) move.
- `Slider.Range`: The filled portion of the track.
- `Slider.Thumbs` or `Slider.Thumb + Slider.HiddenInput`: The draggable handle(s).
- `Slider.ThumbIndicator`: The thumb tooltip.
- `Slider.Hint`: The hint text below the slider.
- `Slider.ErrorText`: The error message below the slider.
- `Slider.Markers` or `Slider.MarkerGroup + Slider.Marker`: The markers along the track.

### Thumbs

If you need more control over the thumbs, you can use the `Slider.Thumb` component instead of the `Slider.Thumbs` shortcut.
Also note that `Slider.Thumbs` will automatically create a range slider when the slider's `value` or `defaultValue` is set accordingly.

```tsx
import {Slider} from "@qualcomm-ui/react/slider"

function RangeSlider() {
  return (
    <Slider.Root defaultValue={[25, 50]}>
      <Slider.ValueText />
      <Slider.Control>
        <Slider.Track>
          <Slider.Range />
        </Slider.Track>
        <Slider.Thumb index={0} name="min">
          <Slider.HiddenInput />
        </Slider.Thumb>
        <Slider.Thumb index={1} name="max">
          <Slider.HiddenInput />
        </Slider.Thumb>
      </Slider.Control>
    </Slider.Root>
  )
}
```

### Thumbs with tooltips

Setting the [tooltip](./#tooltip-2) prop on the `Slider.Thumbs` component is the equivalent of the following composition:

```tsx
import {Slider} from "@qualcomm-ui/react/slider"

function SliderWithTooltip() {
  return (
    <Slider.Root defaultValue={[25, 50]}>
      <Slider.Control>
        <Slider.Track>
          <Slider.Range />
        </Slider.Track>
        <Slider.Thumb index={0}>
          <Slider.HiddenInput />
          <Slider.ThumbIndicator />
        </Slider.Thumb>
        <Slider.Thumb index={1}>
          <Slider.HiddenInput />
          <Slider.ThumbIndicator />
        </Slider.Thumb>
      </Slider.Control>
    </Slider.Root>
  )
}
```

### Markers

The `Markers` component is a convenient shortcut to display custom track markers. But you can also create your own markers using the `Slider.MarkerGroup` and `Slider.Marker` components.

```tsx
import {Slider} from "@qualcomm-ui/react/slider"

function SliderWithCustomMarkers() {
  return (
    <Slider.Root defaultValue={[25, 50]}>
      <Slider.ValueText />
      <Slider.Control>
        <Slider.Track>
          <Slider.Range />
        </Slider.Track>
        <Slider.Thumbs />
      </Slider.Control>
      <Slider.MarkerGroup>
        <Slider.Marker value={0}>0</Slider.Marker>
        <Slider.Marker value={25}>25</Slider.Marker>
        <Slider.Marker value={50}>50</Slider.Marker>
        <Slider.Marker value={75}>75</Slider.Marker>
        <Slider.Marker value={100}>100</Slider.Marker>
      </Slider.MarkerGroup>
    </Slider.Root>
  )
}
```

import {ComponentExplorer, Demo} from "~components/demo"

import * as demos from "./demos"

# {frontmatter.title}

{frontmatter.description}

```tsx
import {Stepper} from "@qualcomm-ui/react/stepper"
```

## Examples

### Linear Mode

The stepper is linear by default ([linear](./#linear) is `true`). Steps must be completed in order.

- Backward navigation is always allowed
- Previously visited steps can be re-clicked without restriction
- Forward navigation is restricted to the immediate next step
- [canGoToStep](./#canGoToStep) can override forward navigation decisions

<Demo component={demos.StepperLinearDemo} name="StepperLinearDemo" />

### Non-linear Mode

Set [linear](./#linear) to `false` to allow accessing any step at any time. Use the [completed](./#completed) prop to manually track which steps are done.

[canGoToStep](./#canGoToStep) applies to all navigation if provided. Otherwise, all navigation is allowed.

<Demo component={demos.StepperNonlinearDemo} name="StepperNonlinearDemo" />

### Icon

Use the `<Stepper.IndicatorIcon>` component to use an icon for each step's indicator.

<Demo name="StepperIconDemo" component={demos.StepperIconDemo} />

### Hint

Add a hint to provide additional context below the step label.

<Demo name="StepperHintDemo" component={demos.StepperHintDemo} />

### Layout & Orientation

Stepper orientation and label placement are controlled through the [orientation](./#orientation) prop.

#### Horizontal

`horizontal` (default): The step list is centered horizontally, and the labels are stacked vertically and centered below the step indicator.

<Demo
  component={demos.StepperHorizontalDemo}
  name="StepperHorizontalDemo"
/>

#### Horizontal Inline

`horizontal-inline` is a variant of `horizontal` that places the step indicator and labels inline. The step items are left-aligned and take the full width of their parent container

<Demo
  component={demos.StepperHorizontalInlineDemo}
  name="StepperHorizontalInlineDemo"
/>

#### Horizontal Bottom Start

`horizontal-bottom-start` is a variant of `horizontal` that places the labels below each step, aligned to the start. The items are left-aligned and take the full width of their parent container.

<Demo
  component={demos.StepperHorizontalBottomStartDemo}
  name="StepperHorizontalBottomStartDemo"
/>

#### Vertical

Set [orientation](./#orientation) to `vertical` to stack the steps vertically. The labels are centered relative to the step indicator.

<Demo name="StepperVerticalDemo" component={demos.StepperVerticalDemo} />

#### Vertical Inline

Set [orientation](./#orientation) to `vertical-inline` to stack the steps vertically while aligning the labels inline with the step indicator.

<Demo
  name="StepperVerticalInlineDemo"
  component={demos.StepperVerticalInlineDemo}
/>

### Controlled State

Use [step](./#step) and [onStepChange](./#onStepChange) to control the active step externally.

<Demo
  expanded
  name="StepperControlledDemo"
  component={demos.StepperControlledDemo}
/>

### Manual Completion

Set [linear](./#linear) to `false` and use the [completed](./#completed) prop to manually control which steps are marked as complete.

<Demo
  expanded
  name="StepperCompletedDemo"
  component={demos.StepperCompletedDemo}
/>

### Pending Steps

Use the [pending](./#pending) prop to mark steps as pending. This is typically used to indicate that a step has been visited but not completed.

<Demo component={demos.StepperPendingDemo} name="StepperPendingDemo" />

### Sizes

The stepper comes in two [sizes](./#size): `sm` and `lg`. The default size is `lg`.

<Demo expanded name="StepperSizesDemo" component={demos.StepperSizesDemo} />

### Validation Examples

#### Non-linear Form

Combine `linear={false}` with per-step validation to let users complete steps in any order. Use the [invalid](./#invalid) and [completed](./#completed) props to track each step's status, and [Stepper.Context](./#stepper-context) to conditionally render a submit action once all steps pass.

<Demo
  expanded
  name="StepperNonlinearFormDemo"
  component={demos.StepperNonlinearFormDemo}
/>

#### Skippable Steps

Use [isStepSkippable](./#isStepSkippable) to mark optional steps that can be bypassed during navigation.

<Demo
  expanded
  name="StepperSkippableStepsDemo"
  component={demos.StepperSkippableStepsDemo}
/>

Source: https://github.com/qualcomm/qualcomm-ui/blob/main/packages/docs/react-docs/src/routes/components+/switch+/_switch.mdx

title: Switch
description: Switches enable users to instantly activate or deactivate features, settings, or options with immediate visual confirmation. The component features a sliding thumb that moves along a track to communicate the current state.
component: Switch
aliases: [toggle, toggle switch]

import {ComponentExplorer, Demo} from "~components/demo"
import * as demos from "./demos"
import {TypeDocProps, TypeDocAttributes} from "@qualcomm-ui/react-mdx/typedoc"

# {frontmatter.title}

{frontmatter.description}

```tsx
import {Switch} from "@qualcomm-ui/react/switch"
```

## Examples

### Simple

Basic switch using the simple API with a label.

<Demo name="SwitchSimpleDemo" component={demos.SwitchSimpleDemo} />

### Composite

::: terms
compound component, composed, subcomponents
:::

Build with the composite API for granular control. This API requires you to provide each subcomponent, but gives you full control over the structure and layout.

<Demo
  name="SwitchCompositeLayoutDemo"
  component={demos.SwitchCompositeLayoutDemo}
/>

### States

::: terms
on, off, true, false
:::

Based on the inputs, the switch will render as checked or unchecked.

<Demo name="SwitchStatesDemo" component={demos.SwitchStatesDemo} />

### Disabled State

::: terms
inactive, read-only
:::

When [disabled](./#disabled) is true, the switch becomes non-interactive and is rendered with reduced opacity to indicate its unavailable state.

<Demo name="SwitchDisabledDemo" component={demos.SwitchDisabledDemo} />

### Sizes

::: terms
small, medium, large
:::

Use the [size](./#size) prop to change the size of the switch. The default size is `md`.

<Demo name="SwitchSizesDemo" component={demos.SwitchSizesDemo} />

### Hint

::: terms
helper text, description, supporting text
:::

Add a hint to provide additional context below the switch.

<Demo name="SwitchHintDemo" component={demos.SwitchHintDemo} />

### Group

::: terms
switch group, field group
:::

Use [SwitchGroup](/components/switch-group) to group related switches with a shared label, hint text, and validation state.

### Controlled State

::: terms
useState, state management, two-way binding
:::

Set the initial value using the [defaultChecked](./#defaultChecked) prop, or use [checked](./#checked) and [onCheckedChange](./#onCheckedChange) to control the value manually. These props follow our [controlled state](/patterns/controlled-state) pattern.

<Demo
  expanded
  name="SwitchControlledDemo"
  component={demos.SwitchControlledDemo}
/>

## Forms

Choose the form library that fits your needs—we've built examples with React Hook Form and Tanstack Form to get you started.

### React Hook Form

::: terms
rhf
:::

Use [React Hook Form](https://react-hook-form.com/) to handle the switch state and validation. [ArkType](https://arktype.io/) works great for schema validation if you need it.

<Demo
  expanded
  name="SwitchReactHookFormDemo"
  component={demos.SwitchReactHookFormDemo}
/>

### Tanstack Form

[Tanstack Form](https://tanstack.com/form/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/basic-concepts) handles switch validation with its built-in validators.

<Demo
  expanded
  name="SwitchTanstackFormDemo"
  component={demos.SwitchTanstackFormDemo}
/>

Tanstack form also supports [ArkType](https://tanstack.com/form/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/validation#validation-through-schema-libraries).

## Composite Guidelines

The composite elements are only intended to be used as direct descendants of the `<Switch.Root>` component.

```tsx
/* Won't work alone ❌ */
<Switch.HiddenInput />
<Switch.Control />

/* Works as expected ✅ */
<Switch.Root>
  <Switch.HiddenInput />
  <Switch.Control />
</Switch.Root>
```

## Shortcuts

### Control and Thumb

The switch control automatically renders the thumb if no child elements are supplied. This:

```tsx
<Switch.Control />
```

is equivalent to this:

```tsx
<Switch.Control>
  <Switch.Thumb />
</Switch.Control>
```

```tsx
import {SwitchGroup} from "@qualcomm-ui/react/switch-group"
```

## Examples

### Simple

Use the simple API to create a switch group using minimal markup.

If you omit the [label](./#label), you should provide an [`aria-label`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Attributes/aria-label) prop to keep your group accessible.

<Demo
  name="SwitchGroupSimpleDemo"
  component={demos.SwitchGroupSimpleDemo}
/>

### Composite

Use the composite API for granular control over the group structure.

<Demo
  name="SwitchGroupCompositeDemo"
  component={demos.SwitchGroupCompositeDemo}
/>

### Size

::: terms
small, medium, large
:::

The [size](./#size-1) prop controls the size of child switches. Available sizes are `sm`, `md` (default), and `lg`.

<Demo name="SwitchGroupSizeDemo" component={demos.SwitchGroupSizeDemo} />

### Orientation

::: terms
vertical, horizontal, row, column
:::

Use the [orientation](./#orientation-1) prop to control the layout direction of the group. Options include:

- `vertical`: switches are laid out in a column (default).
- `horizontal`: switches are laid out in a row.

<Demo
  name="SwitchGroupOrientationDemo"
  component={demos.SwitchGroupOrientationDemo}
/>

### Indented

Set [indented](./#indented-1) to add padding at the start of the group.

<Demo
  name="SwitchGroupIndentedDemo"
  component={demos.SwitchGroupIndentedDemo}
/>

### Hint

::: terms
helper text, description
:::

Use [hint](./#hint-1) to add additional guidance or context to the user below the group.

<Demo name="SwitchGroupHintDemo" component={demos.SwitchGroupHintDemo} />

### Error Text

::: terms
validation, invalid
:::

Set [invalid](./#invalid) and [errorText](./#errorText) to display validation errors. The error text replaces the hint when present.

<Demo name="SwitchGroupErrorDemo" component={demos.SwitchGroupErrorDemo} />

```tsx
import {Tab, Tabs} from "@qualcomm-ui/react/tabs"
```

## Examples

### Horizontal

::: terms
keyboard navigation
:::

The default [orientation](./#orientation) is horizontal. The left and right arrow keys can be used to navigate between tabs.

<Demo name="TabsHorizontalDemo" component={demos.TabsHorizontalDemo} />

### Vertical

::: terms
stacked tabs, sidebar tabs
:::

In vertical [orientation](./#orientation), the up and down arrow keys are used instead.

<Demo name="TabsVerticalDemo" component={demos.TabsVerticalDemo} />

### Icons and variants

Tabs support start and end icons. Customize the variant with the [iconVariant](./#iconVariant) prop. Use the [variant](./#variant) prop to change the appearance of the tab.

<Demo
  wrapperProps={{className: "bg-neutral-02"}}
  name="TabsIconsDemo"
  component={demos.TabsIconsDemo}
/>

### Controlled Value

The tab's active value can be controlled via the [value](./#value), [onValueChange](./#onValueChange), and [defaultValue](./#defaultValue) properties. These props follow our [controlled state](/patterns/controlled-state) pattern.

<Demo
  name="TabsControlledValueDemo"
  component={demos.TabsControlledValueDemo}
/>

### Sizes

#### Line

::: terms
underline tabs, small, medium, large, extra large
:::

The line [variant](./#variant) supports four [sizes](./#size): `sm`, `md`, `lg`, and `xl`

<Demo name="TabsLineSizesDemo" component={demos.TabsLineSizesDemo} />

#### Contained

::: terms
pill tabs, segmented control, small, medium
:::

The contained [variant](./#variant) supports only two sizes: `sm` and `md`

<Demo
  wrapperProps={{className: "bg-neutral-02"}}
  name="TabsContainedSizesDemo"
  component={demos.TabsContainedSizesDemo}
/>

### Lazy Mounted

::: terms
deferred rendering, performance optimization, conditional rendering
:::

Use the [lazyMount](./#lazyMount) and [unmountOnExit](./#unmountOnExit) props to control render behavior for inactive tabs.

<Demo name="TabsLazyMountedDemo" component={demos.TabsLazyMountedDemo} />

### Disabled

Disable specific tabs with the [disabled](./#disabled-1) prop on the `<Tab.Root>` component.

<Demo
  wrapperProps={{className: "bg-neutral-02"}}
  name="TabsDisabledDemo"
  component={demos.TabsDisabledDemo}
/>

### URL Search Parameters

::: terms
deep linking, shareable URL, query string
:::

The following example demonstrates how to render tabs that sync with the URL search parameters using react-router.

<Demo name="TabsLinksDemo" component={demos.TabsLinksDemo} />

### Context

::: terms
programmatic tab selection, imperative API, setValue
:::

Use the `<Tabs.Context>` component to access the tabs API from JSX.

<Demo name="TabsContextDemo" component={demos.TabsContextDemo} />

### Add and Remove Tabs

::: terms
closable tabs, close button, dismissible
:::

Use `<Tab.DismissButton>` to make tabs removable. Combine this with React state to create a dynamic tab interface where users can add and close tabs.

<Demo name="TabsAddRemoveDemo" component={demos.TabsAddRemoveDemo} />
